prompt:
Role and task instructions:
You, Mia, have been asked to play a hug role in your best friend Hannah's wedding. You are the maid of honor and you are asked to give a speech at the reception.

User request:
You are Mia and is the maid of honor and the best friend of the bride, Hannah. Hannah is marrying Andrew. Your task is to compose an entertaining and heartfelt maid of honor speech for a wedding. This speech should blend humor, personal anecdotes, and genuine emotion to celebrate the couple's special day.
The audience will be a diverse group of wedding guests, including family members of varying ages, friends, and acquaintances of the bride and groom. They are gathered to celebrate and are looking forward to enjoying the festivities. Your speech should cater to this joyful and celebratory mood, being relatable and engaging to all attendees.
Remember, the goal of your speech is to entertain while sincerely honoring the bride and groom. It's an opportunity to add to the joy and celebration of their special day.
answer:
Good evening, everyone. For those I haven’t met, I’m Mia, Hannah’s best friend and very proud maid of honor.

Hannah and I have shared years of laughter, long conversations, and the sort of friendship where you can send just one word and know the other person will understand the entire story. She has always been the person who shows up: with a listening ear, a generous heart, and, when needed, an extremely convincing “you’ve got this.”

Hannah, you make the people around you feel seen and loved. I’ve always admired your kindness, your strength, and your ability to find joy in the everyday. Being your friend is one of the great gifts of my life.

Then Andrew came along. It didn’t take long to see how happy you make each other. Andrew, you meet Hannah with warmth, humor, and care—and you love her not just for the wonderful person she is, but in all the little ways that make a life together. Thank you for making my best friend so happy, and for joining the rest of us in being lucky enough to have her in our lives.

The best partnerships aren’t about being exactly alike. They’re about making room for each other, laughing together, and being on the same team when life gets complicated. Hannah and Andrew, you already do that beautifully. May your marriage bring you a lifetime of shared adventures, small daily joys, and plenty of reasons to laugh—especially at each other’s jokes, even the ones you’ve heard before.

Please raise a glass to Hannah and Andrew: to a love that keeps growing, a friendship that lasts, and a very happy life together. Cheers!
